verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. The variable Lean calls y.2 (= x) is the paper's δ_b: SlowFirstOrderEdge.xChart sends w to (w.2, y0 + 3 - Real.log w.1), i.e. log X_b - log X with log X_b = y0 + 3, and FlatCutoff.edge 4 δ = e^{-4/δ^2}, so the Gaussian-flat weight and the constant 4 match exactly. Lean proves more than the first bound of (5.22): profileStress_factorization is an exact identity profileStress = (e^{-4/δ^2}/δ^3) · stressFactor with stressFactor smooth (stressFactor_contDiff), from which |𝒯_1| ≤ C e^{-4/δ^2}δ^{-3} follows by taking C = sup|stressFactor| over the compact collar η ∈ [-1,1], δ ∈ [0,b]; the paper's exponent 3 is Lean's exponent 3. For the derivative bound, profileStress_jets gives one pair (M, N) valid uniformly for all multi-indices of order i ≤ n, which is stronger than the paper's per-index constants C_I, N_I, and it covers joint η-and-δ derivatives on η ∈ [-1,1], 0 < x ≤ b. I did not verify that the N produced by profileStress_jets equals 3 at i = 0, so the sharp exponent in the first bound comes from the factorization, not from the jets theorem.
